EICMA 2026 • Honda Has a Taste of the e-MTB World with the RN0 Motor-Assisted Bicycle
The Airelume 260 Is a Different Kind of Family Travel Trailer, Sleeps Nine Without Slide-Outs
17 photos
Photo: Forest River/ That RV Girl
An old adage says there is beauty in simplicity, and this is valid for many aspects of life. The saying applies even to the RV life, where stripping away excess weight, complicated systems, unnecessary ornamentation, and clutter creates space for more freedom and adventure.
Introduced earlier in 2026 in partnership with dealer Camping World, Forest River’s Airelume range of travel trailers follows precisely this philosophy. Instead of chasing trends and fitting their RVs with features that might end up unused, the company focused on creating a lineup that includes features that campers actually use and that “make everyday camping moments easier and more enjoyable.”
Inspired by customer feedback and designed with intention, the Airelume range aims to strike a balance between quality construction, practical design, and reasonable pricing. In the short time since its introduction, the lineup has already expanded to include 13 floor plans that vary widely in size and configuration, so there is a model for everyone, from solo travelers and couples to large families.
The Airelume 260 is a travel trailer aimed at families or groups of friends with a bunkhouse floor plan that manages to accommodate up to nine people while keeping its weight below 6,400 pounds (2,900 kg). It measures just under 29 feet (8.8 meters) in length and is characterized by refreshing simplicity and practicality.
Photo: Forest River/ That RV Girl While most family-oriented RVs resort to slide-outs or lofts to expand the available square footage and sleeping capacity, the Airelume 260 offers double bunks, a queen bed, and convertible sleeping areas, alongside a kitchen, dinette, and bathroom, in a zero-slideout design. But what makes it even more appealing is that it still offers a residential feel, with practical amenities and details such as a dedicated coffee nook, a sofa built for real legroom, industry-leading countertop, a 60K water heater, and more.
It is a dual-axle travel trailer with a single entrance, and like all the models in the Airelume lineup, it boasts a powder-coated I-beam frame, a Tufflex PVC roof, and an enclosed underbelly. On the outside, it showcases a catchy white and blue color scheme with color-matched fenders and the Airelume badge on the front cap.
The exterior equipment is kept simple and functional, with a pass-through storage compartment at the front, manual stabilizers and a manual tongue jack, accessible propane tanks, and a dedicated battery compartment. There is also a bumper-mounted spare tire at the rear, as well as preparation for an observation camera. The side of the trailer houses the main utility connections and a black tank flush.
Photo: Forest River/ That RV Girl One of the Airelume 260’s strongest suits is the generous sleeping capacity it manages to offer within a relatively compact footprint . As already mentioned, it can accommodate up to nine people without making the interior feel claustrophobic or hard to navigate for daily activities.
Many travel trailers with similar sleeping capacity rely on slide-outs or have a longer body, but this model manages to do it with a clever interior arrangement: a front queen bedroom, a rear bunk area that offers a double-over-double setup, a jackknife sofa that pulls into a bed, and a convertible dinette.
The bunkhouse boasts a clever notched design, just like we’ve seen on the Airelume 265 floor plan , allowing for two spacious sleeping levels, each with lighting and its own window. There’s also storage beneath the bunks and roof vent above that helps with air circulation.
At the other end of the trailer, the main bedroom is a more conventional sleeping space with a walk-around queen bed flanked by windows with privacy shades, bedside shelves, a wardrobe, and some deep cubbies for additional closet space. There is also under-bed storage and interior access to the front pass-through compartment.
Photo: Forest River/ That RV Girl The only caveat regarding this arrangements is the lack of privacy. There are no full walls and solid doors to separate the central common living area of the trailer from the rear and front sleeping spaces. However, for the main bedroom, there is a partial wall that creates a sense of separation and owners can later add a curtain for some privacy.
The single-block kitchen is located on the campsite and comes with some features meant to make the compact space more convenient to use. I’m referring, of course, to the dedicated Coffee Corner with K-Cup holder, cubbies for storing supplies, hooks for hanging cups, and an electrical outlet for a coffee maker. There is even an overhead microwave in this area.
The kitchen is also fully functional and includes a deep stainless-steel sink, two gas burners, and a 12-volt refrigerator and freezer. The dining area is a traditional booth dinette placed under a large window, while a nearby TV mount comes in handy if your idea of entertainment involves watching some popular shows.
Photo: Forest River/ That RV Girl The bathroom is compact , as it shares the rear of the trailer with the bunk area, but it includes all the basics. It features a Thetford toilet, vanity sink, mirror, storage cabinets, and a shower with a curtain and integrated shelves for toiletries.
In terms of styling, the interior has a bright, modern residential feel with European-style flat-front cabinetry, seamless pressed countertops, woven cloth-style upholstery, and easy-to-clean vinyl flooring.
As for the numbers you need to know, this RV has a dry weight of 4,399 pounds (1,995 kg) and a GVWR rating of 6,399 pounds (2,902 kg), which leaves 2,000 pounds (907 kg) of cargo carrying capacity. It holds a fresh water tank of 39 gallons (147 liters), as well as gray and black water tanks, each with a capacity of 30 gallons (113 liters). Though it’s mainly designed for campground use, it comes pre-wired for solar expansion, supporting up to 500 watts.
No MSRP is listed on the official page of the Airlume 260 travel trailer , but actual dealer prices range between $18,499 and $27,199.
